newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts sink, grapple for support after auction.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts sink, grapple for support after auction.

text.p: 1620 GMT - UK gilts sank to fresh two-week lows after an auction of stock due 2021 attracted cover of just 1.29 times with a lengthy yield tail. Futures slipped through key support at 112-28 and struggled to find support lower down.
* June gilt future down 1-2/32 on day at 111-28/32.

The gilt future moved up from 112-28 two weeks ago after Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown announced the Bank of England would be free to set interest rates. It rose so fast that few other footholds were established on the way up.

Gilts analysts had said a central bank with control of monetary policy should guarantee lower long-term inflation and therefore boost longer-dated gilts. But Thursday's auction of 1.5 billion of 8.0 percent gilts due 2021 attracted cover just 1.29 times with a yield tail of four basis points, suggesting much of the stock was sold at a cut price.

"The current theory is that people had already bought their fill at the long end. We ran out of investors," said Steve Scott, gilts analyst at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson. "But I was still surprised how poorly it went."

The gilt/Bund spread closed at 149 basis points compared with 142 on Wednesday. Scott said that at more than 10 basis points wider than its narrowest point since Labour was swept to power on May 1, it should attract buyers back to gilts soon. The trader agreed: "We have seen people switching longer after the auction. The long end has fallen like a stone today and there's better value there than there was a week ago."
Gilts were not helped by German Bunds skidding lower after breaking through support levels, while weakness in the U.S. Treasuries market also undermined sentiment.

June short sterling also weakened before recovering slightly to end the day at 93.43, down 0.01. This implies official interest rates of around 6.60 percent compared with 6.25 percent at present. -- Paul Carrel, London newsroom +44 171 542 7708
